# Cloud Console Hardening — epic charter

Successor to the Cloud GUI Remake epic (SEALED 2026-07-21, PR #5226). Inherited 58 re-parented
survivors + 10 natively-filed rows = 69 open children. This file is the epic's memory: every wave
reads it first.

## Vision

**The console stops lying.**

Nearly every row worth building names a place where the console tells somebody something untrue.
It tells the network 40 requests are 5. It tells every user their session came from `172.18.0.1`
(measured: 48 of 49 production session rows). It tells the access log a bearer token is part of a
URL. It tells the rate limiter all users are one user. It tells a HEAD prober a session token in a
`location` header. It tells the developer a revoke succeeded on a route the mock never called, and
that a CSS check passed on code it just deleted.

After this epic, what the console SHOWS and what it DOES match — and the instruments asserting that
match are themselves able to fail.

This is also the epic's **triage predicate**: a row survives if it names a claim/reality divergence;
it closes when the divergence is gone. That single predicate generates all three movements, because
a lying harness and a lying rate limiter are the same defect class pointed at different audiences.

## Standing laws

0. **A wave may not end with more live rows than it began, and instrument residue is filed under the
   SUCCESSOR, never here.** Added wave 12 (D146). This epic keeps rows whose divergence is visible on
   a console surface a person can reach; every gate, generator, harness, required-checks or
   ledger-hygiene row belongs to `bp-cloud-console-instruments-charter.md`. **That destination is the
   TASK `cch-instruments-epic`, not the file** — file with
   `parent_id: cch-instruments-epic` AT CREATE TIME (a create, never a re-parent).
   **[CORRECTED 2026-08-06, wave 35 — D403.** This clause used to read *"the charter document is
   stranded on unmerged PR #8500"*. **#8500 MERGED 2026-08-02T18:06:03Z (`0b425c7e8`) and
   `.claude/workflows/bp-cloud-console-instruments-charter.md` IS on `origin/main`.** The filing rule
   is unchanged and still correct — the task is the destination, not the file — but its stated REASON
   was a state the law stopped measuring, inside the epic about asserting states you cannot support.**]**
   **RESIDUE MEASUREMENT
   PROTOCOL**: count live rows from the seal predicate's own roster read at FIRST CLAIM and again at
   DEBRIEF; a wave that nets positive states the number and names what it repays. `bp task get`'s
   `child_count` is a LIFETIME total on both epics (a cancel does not decrement it) and its open
   count includes `drafts.*` — at wave 16's first claim the predicate read **196 published children:
   112 done / 65 open / 18 cancelled / 1 considering**, while `bp task get` said 200/67. Quote 65.
   The two halves are one law: without the filing half, the split is undone by the next wave's own
   residue. **Live-row counts
   are quoted from the seal predicate's OWN denominator** — its roster read returns published children
   only, so `drafts.*` entries are duplicates, never rows (D105), and a census that counts them
   overstates. **And a review owed before merge is FILED AS A ROW** — that law was written in wave 9,
   kept only as Paper prose in waves 9, 10 and 11, and was 0-for-3 until wave 12 filed
   `cch-w12-bl-independent-review-owed-wave-12`.

1. **Cite MERGE SHAs, never branch SHAs.** `origin/main` is a linear squash chain, so
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch-head> origin/main` always false-negatives. Get the SHA from
   `gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit`. Inherited from the GUI epic; re-proved this wave (five
   worktree branches read NOT-merged while their PRs were MERGED).
2. **No row closes without a reproduction attempt.** The false-done pattern (11 tasks fake-done,
   then reopened) is this repo's most expensive recurring defect. A merge SHA plus a `file:line` is
   the minimum evidence.
3. **The census is L4, not L1.** The epic description carries a six-band disposition census written
   at seal round 10. It is a *hypothesis ranking*. Wave 1 measured it: roughly one third was stale —
   always in the SAFE direction (rows more done than claimed, never less). Keep the bands; re-derive
   truth values before building.
4. **Roster reads have exactly two safe routes.** `GET /v1/tasks?filter[parent_id]=…` silently
   returns foreign rows with a 200 (re-proved 2026-07-21: 0 of 15 rows in a default page actually
   carried the requested parent) — never source a roster from it. Use `bp task get <epic> -o json` →
   `.children` for the roster, and a per-row `bp task get <id>` for evidence. `.children` carries no
   `updated_at`/`closed_at`, so it cannot answer close-time questions. `bp task ls` has no
   `--parent` flag.

   **Wave-2 correction — the `/v1/data/query` bracket story was wrong.** Wave 1 recorded that bare
   curl with unencoded `filter[parent_id]` brackets returns "200 with 140 rows from another epic".
   Executably refuted: that command never reaches the server. curl's own URL-globbing parser rejects
   `[parent_id]` as a malformed range and **aborts client-side with exit 3 (`bad range in URL`)**,
   writing no output file. Under `curl -g` or Python urllib — where literal brackets really do go on
   the wire — `/v1/data/query/production/task` filters **correctly** (91/91 rows, matching
   `.children` exactly). The `140` traces to `gr-p5r5-successor-seal`'s roster-delta note for the
   *predecessor* GUI-Remake epic. The real hazard on this route is a **stale-file misread**: a script
   that reuses a fixed output path and skips the exit-code check reports yesterday's bytes as a live
   200. So the rule is not "encode the brackets or get wrong rows" — it is:

   ```bash
   # Route A (preferred): bp task get <epic> -o json | .children
   # Route B (raw HTTP): -G --data-urlencode, fresh mktemp path, and CHECK THE EXIT CODE.
   OUT=$(mktemp)
   if curl -sf -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" \
        'https://guerrilla.barkpark.cloud/v1/data/query/production/task' \
        --data-urlencode 'filter[parent_id]=cloud-console-hardening-epic' \
        --data-urlencode 'limit=500' -o "$OUT"; then
     python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$OUT'))['result']['count'])"
   else
     echo "FETCH FAILED (curl exit $?) — \$OUT was NOT written by this run; do not read it" >&2
   fi
   ```
   The bracket-abort is generic to curl, not to `parent_id`: `filter[lifecycle_status]` and
   `filter[type]` reproduce it identically.

7. **A gate's classification is a claim like any other — write it, never cite it.** Wave 2 caught
   itself asserting "per the repo's standing advisory classification for Vercel" when
   `grep -in vercel docs/ops/merge-gates.md` returns nothing and
   `gr-blk-vercel-checks-ungoverned` is 0/2. Asserting a rule that does not exist, inside the epic
   whose frame is "the console stops lying", is the same defect pointed at ourselves. If a gate needs
   a classification, land the sentence.
5. **MERGE-GATED criteria are stamped by the LEAD, never the builder.** `autostamp_merge_gate`
   (`api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex`) only fires on a criterion literally carrying
   `merge_gate: true`. **CORRECTED AT WAVE 66 (D801): the flag is NOT out of fence and NOT
   unwritable — it is an AUTHORING choice this epic controls.** `Validation.check_optional_map_list`
   is shape-only with no per-entry key allowlist, and `Internal.apply_entry_update/2` `Map.put`s
   INTO the stored entry, so the marker survives create, stamp and close. `bp task create --set
   'acceptance_criteria:=[{"criterion":"MERGE-GATED …","met":false,"merge_gate":true}]'` emits it
   today (raw typed-JSON passthrough, no key filtering). **Author the boolean beside the MERGE-GATED
   wording on every gate criterion this epic files.** Retrofit onto an ALREADY-FILED row is
   create-time-asymmetric — `Params.parse_criteria_entry/1` rebuilds each update from a four-key
   allowlist (`index`/`met`/`evidence`/`criterion`), so adding it later needs a raw whole-array
   `/v1/data/mutate` patch, which is a read-modify-write with NO rev-CAS and is MEASURED LOSSY.
   **Never bulk-retrofit; author at birth.** The lead closes the gate with
   `bp task close … --set 'landed:={"prs":[N]}'`, which DEDUCTS the marked indices and mints no
   `criteria_override` at all (D797).
6. **Never branch from the primary checkout.** `/Volumes/SATECHI/github/barkpark` is shared by many
   concurrent sessions, is routinely ahead/behind origin, and at the time of writing carried an
   uncommitted comment-corrupting edit to `cloud/priv/static/app.css`. Cut every branch from
   `origin/main` explicitly; diff files against `git show origin/main:<path>`, never a working tree.
   Do not clean, stash, or reset that checkout — it holds other sessions' work.

9. **The GUI-remake GR set binds this epic — stated here because it was never stated.** Added wave 16
   (D191). `GR11`/`GR25`/`GR116` are defined only in `bp-cloud-gui-remake-charter.md` (`:25`, `:40`,
   `:502`); this charter's preamble inherits ROWS, not RULES, so every GR citation in D153/D157/D165
   and in `app.css:2196`/`:2270` was formally unanchored. It is anchored now. GR25 governs the scope:
   the quarantine forbids EDITING the four pill-family rule blocks (`status-pill`, `dep-pill`,
   `tlv-badge`, `badge`/`fresh-badge`), never CONSUMING them; wrappers (`.fleet-status`,
   `.fleet-main`, `.rail-row`) are outside it. Any slice that must edit inside the fence needs its own
   D157-shaped carve-out ruling, argued as an ADD rather than a restyle.

- `.github/workflows/console-harness.yml` — CI wiring for console instruments.

**Wave-33 widening — ONE SUBJECT, FOUR AGGREGATOR FILES + ONE NAMED GUARD SCRIPT (D377).**

closed by *"not to be widened"* and `elixir.yml` is absent from it — verified by reading the sentence,

sentence. Law 0 is NOT suspended: this is a WISH-SCOPED exception (the wave's own wish names *"their
gates"* explicitly), and every OTHER gate/instrument row this wave surfaced is filed under

  DEFINE the current trigger verbatim — so this ADD amends another epic's closed, evidenced
  contract, and says so rather than pretending the missing lead check was an oversight.
  **Concurrency, measured at Decide (2026-08-10):** ZERO open PRs and ZERO of 592 worktrees hold
  `close.ex` or `stamp.ex` dirty; deploy-reliability wave 34 is live and holds only
  `deploy_ledger.ex`, `deploy_ledger_test.exs` and `crown-reconcile*`.
**Not to be widened** — a further file or subject requires its own numbered sentence.

**Out of fence, hands off:** `tooling/grip/` (truth-grip **wave 5** running, PR #5314), `scripts/pds-*`
and `api/lib/barkpark/tenancy/` (PDS **wave 15** running — paper `pds-wave-15-2026-07-21`; wave 2's
survey wrongly reported no wave 15 exists, it does).

## The dark crown

`PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS` is unset on prod. It lives in a gitignored `.env`; zero deploy scripts
reference it; **no commit can set it**. Every authenticated user gets 403 on the operator console.
This is a HUMAN GATE belonging to the repo owner. Note it where relevant; never build around it,
fake it, or file work that depends on it being lit. Same disposition for the QR live-scan proof.

## Decisions

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Keep the six-band census; re-verify rather than re-derive it | A prior Fable wrote it with full seal context; re-deriving burns the whole budget reproducing a worse version. Re-verification is the cheap part and the only part genuinely missing. |
| D2 | Refetch storm is fixed by **scope-narrowing**, never debounce | Repeats are evenly spaced (1 cold boot + 7 ticks = 40, reproduced from code alone), so a time window suppresses nothing. Four registered types funnel into one 5-endpoint `loadOverview()`. |
| D3 | The narrowing must also cover the `barkpark.*` **prefix fallback** | `app.js:12076` routes ANY unregistered `barkpark.*` type into the same monolith; a synthetic `barkpark.unknown_skew` fired the full 5. Enumerating the four known types leaves the skew path storming. |
| D4 | The refetch protective test fixture must carry **≥1 instance** | An empty fleet short-circuits `loadOverview()` to 2 requests; an empty-fleet fixture would assert "2" and pass forever while the storm rages for every real user. Vacuous green by construction. |
| D5 | Peer-IP: **PIN** the gateway, do not widen to `172.16/12` | Measured: widening let peer `{172,18,0,77}` forge `203.0.113.5`. `cloud-postfix-1` sits on `172.18.0.2` publishing `0.0.0.0:587` — widening hands an internet-facing SMTP container the ability to forge any client's IP and rate-limit bucket. |
| D6 | The pin ships with a compose `networks:` subnet block **in the same PR** | `docker-compose.yml` has no `networks:` block at all; the subnet is allocation-order-dependent (it landed on `.18` only because the default bridge took `.17`). A bare hardcoded tuple rots silently into a no-op with a test asserting it works. |
| D7 | Do **not** touch RemoteIp's `proxies:` list | Measured: widening `loopback_peer?/1` alone is sufficient. RemoteIp resolves from the header chain and never consults `conn.remote_ip`; a builder reasoning from peer-as-last-hop makes a wrong second edit. |
| D8 | SSE ticket: **strict single-use + a client reconnect rewrite** (option b) | Measured in headless Chrome: ANY 401 is terminal (`readyState 2`, browser never retries again). Short-TTL multi-connect shares the identical cliff on TTL expiry, so the client change is mandatory under BOTH designs — and (b) is strictly stronger security for the same client work. |
| D9 | The SSE slice must add a **fourth liveness-chip state** | The chip documents exactly three states and shows `reconnecting` whenever `evtErrored`, which after a 401 is permanently false. Fixing the leak without it trades a security defect for an honesty defect — inside an epic whose frame is "the console stops lying". |
| D10 | Remint on `readyState 0`, never rely on native retry | Under strict single-use the browser's own retry is a guaranteed 401: ~3.0s of dead stream per flap plus one 401 per flap in the access log (noise that reads like credential stuffing). |
| D11 | HEAD fix is a **router-level deny-list plug placed BEFORE `plug(Plug.Head)`** | `Plug.Head.call/2` is `%{conn \| method: "GET"}` and stashes nothing — by the time control reaches the route, HEAD-ness is destroyed, so per-route short-circuits are impossible, not merely inferior. One greppable list is mutation-testable; a scatter of route-local guards is not. |
| D12 | Answer **405 with `allow: GET`**, not 404 | 404 is the lie that `plug(Plug.Head)` (#4481) was landed to remove. "This path exists, that method is refused" is the honest answer. |
| D13 | Deny-list, not opt-in route tagging | Opt-in requires auditing all 56 GETs now plus every future one, and inverts the default so a forgotten new route silently 404s again. Deny-list fails open on a NEW mutating GET — the milder failure. |
| D14 | Match on `conn.path_info` segment lists, never a string prefix | The initiator and callback share a prefix and `path_params` are unpopulated at plug time (this runs before `:match`); a `starts_with?` guard is either over- or under-broad. |
| D15 | The HEAD slice also **prunes `oauth_states`** | Both GET legs `Repo.insert!` a row per unauthenticated hit and the ONLY delete anywhere is the single-row `consume_state`. No reaper references `OAuth.State`; the Oban crontab schedules none. Unauthenticated unbounded table growth. |
| D16 | Frame slice D as a **response-header leak**, not CWE-598 | The token rides the Location *fragment*, so it does not propagate via Referer or the next hop's access log. Writing CWE-598 into the brief makes a builder fix the wrong thing. |
| D17 | cssom-parity wires as a **separate Node-22 job**, not a fourth step | `console-unit` pins `node-version: 20`; the instrument needs global `WebSocket` (Node 22+). Bumping the whole job would silently change the runtime under two currently-working gates to buy nothing. |
| D18 | No `setup-chrome` action; set `CHROME=/usr/bin/google-chrome` explicitly | Proven on a real runner (PR #5242, run 29801714262): ubuntu-latest ships Chrome 150 at all four candidate paths, parity PASS in 5.9s. `findChrome()` honours `CHROME` but NOT the runner's own `CHROME_BIN`. Pinning turns a future missing binary into an honest exit-2 guard instead of a silent fallthrough. |
| D19 | The wiring must make an env failure exit **2 (guard)**, not 1 (miss) | Under Node 20 the instrument prints `!! PARITY ERROR: WebSocket is not defined` and exits **1** — a misconfigured runner reds the PR with a message that reads like a stylesheet defect. Self-defeating for this epic. |
| D20 | Assert a minimum authored-rule-head **count floor** | Mutation-proving found a blind spot: INSERTING a stray `/*` passes with MISSES 0 (both sides swallow symmetrically, 1201→1188). The gate is proven able to fail only for the de-opened direction. One line closes the hole. |
| D21 | Fix the emit-marker fence in **`emit.mjs`**, not via `check.mjs`-vs-origin/main | `evaluate()` already computes `current` and `expected` in the same pass and knows `drift` before `writeFileSync` — zero new I/O. `check.mjs` compares `build()` to itself after a write (tautological PASS) and a git-diff variant is after-the-fact DETECTION of an already-destroyed file, plus a new external dep in a repo that runs out of worktrees. |
| D22 | Guard the ledger bypass at **both** patch clauses, keyed on `source:` | The compound clause (`:266`) is exploitable via its OWN `set` merge, independently of the plain clause (`:298`); guarding one leaves the other fully open. `source: :sync`/`:api` is already threaded AND read with a safe default — no new plumbing. |
| D23 | Do not reopen `gr-blk-shootsh-scen-suggester` | Its successor `gr-bl-shootsh-scen-suggester-false-done` is already open under this epic. Blind reopening creates a duplicate pair for one fix. Land under the successor; reference the original when disposing of it. |
| D24 | Do not re-parent `gr-blk-studio-presence-perf-flake` | L1-verified: its `parent_id` is already `task-96a908af98698118` ("Felix pristine initiative"), exactly where the epic's own criterion 1 sends it. Stamp the evidence; leave it. |
| D25 | **Wave 1's "AFTER X merges" serialization is RETIRED.** HEAD and SSE build in parallel from `origin/main` | It was file-truth (three slices touch one 10k-line router) mistaken for semantic dependency. Proven by an actual merge, not line arithmetic: all four stranded branches merge into `origin/main` with **exit 0, zero CONFLICT lines, and a byte-identical tree in reverse order**. The whole peer-ip change is ONE hunk `@@ -349,34 +349,81 @@`, so `plug(Plug.Head)` stays at **284 unchanged** and everything below shifts exactly **+47**. The ordering cost is paid once, at merge, by the lead. |
| D26 | The joint-defect fence is **"the mint PATH has no GET route"**, NOT "the mint is a POST" | The lead's stated mechanism is wrong and the wrong version does not protect. `Plug.Head` rewrites HEAD→GET *unconditionally, before matching*; it has no notion of POST. Counterexample measured: `HEAD /v1/tokens` returns **401, not 404**, because `get "/v1/tokens"` exists beside the POST — and authenticated, it returns **200 with 0 PATs created**, having reached the *list* handler. POST-only 404s only because no GET clause matches. A future `get "/v1/auth/sse-ticket"` would silently reopen the trap while every route was still a POST. |
| D27 | SSE mint route: **`post "/v1/auth/sse-ticket"` at `router.ex:1283`** | Between `delete "/v1/auth/logout"` (ends :1282) and the `# GET /v1/account/sessions` comment (:1284) — the authenticated session-lifecycle cluster, authenticated by the session bearer exactly as logout is, ~137 lines above its consumer `get "/v1/events"` (:1420). `POST /v1/tokens` (:3921) is the exact sibling shape. No `get` exists at that path, so D26 holds. |
| D28 | **The consume is MATCHED-ROW-ONLY. Do not copy the prescribed template.** | The wave-1 brief orders the builder to copy `reset_password_by_token`'s consume. Measured: it calls `revoke_reset_tokens(uid, now)` whose WHERE is `user_id + context + is_nil(revoked_at)` — **no `token_hash`** — so consuming one token revokes every live sibling (proven: 2 live → consume 1 → other stamped, count 2→0). The reset *mint* supersedes too. Under D10's remint that is a **two-tab mutual-eviction storm**: tab B mints → A's ticket dies → A 401s → A remints → B dies → forever, one 401 per iteration, the exact log noise D10 exists to prevent. Sibling-wide is right for `reset` (a credential-reset *event*, one link at a time); an SSE ticket is a *per-connection* artifact and the user legitimately holds one per tab. |
| D29 | Take **mint from `2fa_pending`, verify from `verify_user_session_token`, consume from NEITHER** | All three prescribed templates were measured. `create_two_factor_pending_token` is matched-row-only (2 mints → 2 live, both verify) — safe. `delete_two_factor_pending_tokens` is `delete_all` by user_id — sibling-wide. And `verify_two_factor_pending_token` **does not filter `revoked_at`** (proven: a token stamped `revoked_at` still verifies), so a builder copying it ships a ticket whose single-use guarantee is unenforceable. `verify_user_session_token` (:548-568) filters context + `revoked_at` + `expires_at` and is the correct verify. |
| D30 | TTL = **60 seconds**, as `@sse_ticket_validity_seconds 60` (seconds, not the house `*_minutes`) | The live window is only mint→connect: an XHR POST returns it and `new EventSource(...)` opens within one RTT. 20× Chrome's measured ~3000ms retry, satisfying criterion 7's "do not tune tightly against 3s". Shortest-lived credential in the codebase (`@two_factor_pending_minutes 5`, `@state_ttl_seconds 600`, reset 60min, sessions 30d) — correct for a single-use credential consumed in one RTT. Expiry is **self-healing** under D10 (one extra mint round-trip, never a dead stream), so "too short" is bounded and invisible and there is no reason to buy margin. Minutes-granularity invites "round up to 5" and a silent 5× exposure. |
| D31 | **`cloud/priv/static/app.css` joins the SSE slice's fence** | D9's fourth state does not render "unstyled" — it renders **grey**, which is worse, because grey is plausible. Measured in headless Chrome against `origin/main`: a fourth `data-state` matches **0 author rules** and falls back to `.live-dot { background: var(--dim) }` = `rgb(95,106,123)` — a static neutral dot, **visually calmer than the less-severe `reconnecting`** (amber + `live-breathe` animation + amber chip). The most severe state would paint the calmest. `--danger`/`--danger-soft` exist in both light (:69-70) and dark (:106-107) token blocks, so the rule is append-only with zero token edits. |
| D32 | The decisive argument for D31 is the **gate gap**, not the pixel | No gate catches a missing attribute-state rule. `__css_check` E2 extracts only class emissions (`/\.className\s*=\s*"…"/`, `/classList\.(?:add\|remove\|toggle)\(…/`); the chip sets state via `chip.setAttribute("data-state", state)` (app.js:11871), invisible to both regexes. `cssom-parity.mjs` contains **zero** `data-state` references — it proves authored rules reach the browser, never that emitted states have rules. A builder shipping the fourth state without app.css gets a **fully green board on a dead-looking state**: a false green on the fix for a false green. |
| D33 | The SSE slice must widen `__bpTestHook` and add a **closed-enum** test | Measured vacuous-green: `liveDotState`'s 4 existing tests are pure 3-arg equality checks and **no test asserts the return is a closed set**, so JS's permissive arity keeps them all green after a 4th state lands — `node --test` would report green while asserting zero new behaviour. Worse, the DOM assertions are *unwritable today*: `renderLivenessChip()` takes zero params and reads `evtErrored`/`lastEventMs` from private closure state with no setter, and `LIVE_CHIP_COPY`/`LIVE_CHIP_ARIA` are not exported at all. Also: an unknown state falls through `LIVE_CHIP_COPY[state] \|\| "Live"` (:11874) and `LIVE_CHIP_ARIA[state] \|\| "Live updates"` (:11881) — the chip **announcing "Live" over a permanently dead stream**. |
| D34 | The HEAD deny-list **does not grow**, and the floor is **45, not ~36** | Measured over the real `Plug.Head` pipeline: every authenticated GET writes `user_tokens.last_used_at` — **unthrottled** on the session path (`touch_last_used/2` is a bare `update_all`, two HEADs 11ms apart both wrote), throttled to 60s on the PAT path. Census: 56 GETs, 50 authenticated, 5 agent/worker → **45 writers**. The `~36` figure could not be reproduced by any method and is **retired**, not reconciled; the undercount came from 9 routes authenticating only via local wrappers (`with_team_role`, `with_team_site`, `require_user_sse`, `proxy_instance_webhook`) that a grep for `Auth.require_` cannot see. Denying HEAD across 80% of the API reinstates the 404 lie #4481 removed. |
| D35 | The write is not even gated on **authorization** — say so in the evidence | Unclaimed by anyone before wave 2: `HEAD /v1/operator/fleet` with a valid session and a non-operator email answers **403 and still moved `last_used_at`**, because `require_platform_operator/2` calls `require_user/2` first. The touch is a property of *authentication*, not of any route, so there is no subset to carve out. This sharpens D34 rather than weakening it. |
| D36 | Ledger guard extends to `createOrReplace` + `replace` only; **`create`/`createIfNotExists` are EXEMPT by structure** | Measured on all four: `createOrReplace` and `replace` close an existing claimed open task unfenced; `create` returns `{:error, :conflict}` and `createIfNotExists` a silent `noop`. The exemption is structural, not preference: **there is no prior revision on a fresh create**, so D22's `ifRevisionID` escape hatch is undefined and the same guard shape degrades from *fence* to *unconditional ban* — breaking importers the substrate explicitly anticipates (migration `20260528100000`). `existing == nil -> :ok` expresses the whole fork. |
| D37 | These two doors **erase the claimant**, and `ifRevisionID` does not save it — so the guard must also refuse a claim-drop | Strictly larger blast radius than the patch door D22 fences. The patch clause computes `merged = existing.content \|> Map.merge(set)`, so `claim` **survives**; `createOrReplace`/`replace` write `attrs["content"]` **wholesale**, so `after = {"done", nil}` — the claim is *gone*, not stale. Measured: with a **correct** `ifRevisionID` the result is still `lifecycle="done" claim=nil`. Rev is a concurrency fence, never an attribution one. The row is then permanently uncloseable through the sanctioned path (`Tasks.Close` rejects an already-terminal row as `stale_claim`). |
| D38 | The click oracle is **BUILT**, and its scope is the enumerated **8 unfixtured DELETEs**, not the charter's "six" | Prototyped and run: +184/−10 across two files, all 86 pre-existing scenarios still green, and the decisive mutation — changing the per-row Revoke from `addEventListener("click")` to `("mousedown")`, a genuinely dead button with **every source string preserved** — is caught by the oracle (exit 1) and **missed by the 9,074-line `__app.test.mjs` (exit 0)**. That is the capability gap: existing guards assert source strings, this one asserts behaviour. The charter's "six" matches the count of routes that *have* fixtures; there are **14** `api("DELETE"…)` call sites and **8** unfixtured. |
| D39 | The oracle's per-row leg needs a **stateful** fixture, or it plants the defect it exists to remove | Measured limitation: disabling the per-row DELETE fixture stays **green**, because app.js's success arm only calls `loadSessions()` with no toast, so a stateless `route()` returns a byte-identical list. Only revoke-*all* interpolates a server value (`r.data.revoked \|\| 0`) and is text-observable. Shipping the per-row leg as "covered" would be a second false green **inside the anti-false-green slice**. Require a per-boot session store so the list shrinks 2→1. |
| D40 | The sibling-class law is **narrowed to enforcement mechanisms**, not universal | Proposed as "every slice states the CLASS its fix covers and the siblings it does NOT". Only 3 of 6 wave-1 residue rows are genuinely instance-vs-class; two do not fit at all (`cch-w1-emit-fence-regression-test` is a *reflexive* gap — the fence has no test proving it can fail; `cch-bl-overview-subscription-band-stale` is an adjacent pre-existing bug w1 never touched). Stating it universally would **force false evidence onto two slices** — the exact defect this epic removes. Ratified form: **every enforcement mechanism states its own coverage boundary.** `__css_check` E2's boundary (class emission only, attribute-driven state is OUT) is the cheapest first payment. |
| D41 | **A coverage boundary must be MACHINE-CHECKED. A comment is not a tripwire.** This COMPLETES D40 by citing `bp-honest-gates` D1/D5/D11 — it is not an independent ruling | D40 required a boundary to be *stated*. Wave 3 proved stating is not sufficient: the HEAD fence's boundary comment (`router.ex:501`, "this list fences exactly TWO routes… 2 is a FLOOR, not a ceiling") went factually wrong **two commits later, inside the same wave**, from that wave's own sibling slice. Careful, scoped, hedged prose still decayed — because prose cannot ratchet. This law already exists in the repo and must be cited, never re-minted: `bp-honest-gates` **D1** (cause + population + ratchet; a fix without a ratchet regrows, citing a documented-boundary-went-stale case), **D5** (a hand-maintained key list mis-matches both ways — ban the SHAPE, do not enumerate), **D11** (where a full structural predicate is too expensive, a committed baseline count CI forbids increasing is the sanctioned fallback). `truth-grip`'s `screen.mjs` is a shipped implementation of the same law; the citation could not be re-located in this workspace's charter copy, so it is recorded as corroboration, not evidence. |
| D42 | **The HEAD-burns-ticket defect is REAL, PROVEN BY EXECUTION, and the one-line deny clause closes it with zero collateral** | Not a code reading. On a four-way composite of the wave-2 PR heads: `HEAD /v1/events?ticket=<live>` answers **422** (auth SUCCEEDED — the teamless discriminator), stamps `revoked_at`, and the user's subsequent legitimate `GET` gets **401**. `defp side_effecting_get?(["v1","events"]), do: true` → HEAD **405 + allow: GET**, `revoked_at = nil`, legitimate GET **422**. Mutation-killed BOTH directions (a probe asserting the broken behaviour positively went GREEN pre-fix, RED post-fix). Full suite 2182→**2188 tests, 0 failures** (+6 = exactly the new file). Architecturally right, not merely adequate: `consume_sse_ticket/1` takes a bare binary (`accounts.ex:2047`) and is structurally method-blind; `Plug.Head` rewrites the method and stashes nothing; the fence at `:304` is the LAST layer that still sees HEAD-ness and halts before `plug(:match)`, so the 405 costs zero DB access. Threading `conn` into `Accounts` would break the layering. `consume_sse_ticket` has exactly ONE call site in `lib/`, so one clause is SUFFICIENT, not a sample. |
| D43 | **Severity is PROVENANCE, not CVSS. The instance is PREVENTIVE; the tripwire carries the law** | Two independent sweeps agree: **nothing first-party HEADs this console.** The only real monitor (Uptime Kuma) targets the legacy `api/` app on :4000 with GETs; the deploy gate and `verify.ex` use GET; no `Req.head` in `cloud/lib`; no docker healthcheck on app services; `gr-backlog-head-requests`' own brief cites only an internal surveyor's `curl -sI` as the measured trigger. So there is no standing exploitation pressure and the 405 breaks no known consumer. That does **not** weaken the row: this is an **ACCEPTED RISK (D13, in writing) that fired inside the wave that accepted it, from that wave's own sibling slice.** That justifies the tripwire regardless of the instance's exploitability. Argue severity from the mechanism, never from an observed prober. |
| D44 | **`cch-bl-head-denylist-tripwire`'s AC#1 was VACUOUS and is REWRITTEN. The check is a D11 census pin, NOT a Repo-write detector** | The criterion as filed demanded enumerating "router GET clauses whose bodies reach a **Repo write**, directly or one call deep." **That set is EMPTY** — measured: 0 of 62 GET routes reach a `Repo.` write at depth 0 or 1. The entire 10,507-line router has **five** textual `Repo.` refs: one comment, one `Repo.preload` (a read), a `transaction`/`rollback` pair no GET reaches, and one `get_by_uuid` (a read). Every write goes through a context module — the 62 GET blocks reach **103 distinct callees across 29 modules** at depth-1. A check built to AC#1 enumerates ∅, passes forever, and is a textbook vacuous green: **the exact disease this epic exists to remove.** Replaced by a census pin (`{total, session, agent_or_worker, public}` + the deny-clause set), which satisfies the old AC#3 for free — it never asks about writes, so it never has to exclude the auth path. |
| D45 | **Do NOT build an AST walker. Corrected regex-over-source is EXACT, and AST buys nothing** | Measured head-to-head. A `Code.string_to_quoted!` + `Macro.prewalk` census (27ms parse + 2ms walk) is **route-for-route IDENTICAL** to the regex census — `diff` of the two 62-row TSVs is empty. The accuracy problem was never syntax; regex parses this file perfectly. The prior probe's `/v1/me` + `/v1/audit` misclassification was the **end-matcher variant**, root-caused: strict `^  end` = **0/56 wrong**; `^\s*end$` truncates 44; "scan to next route macro" overshoots all 56 and swallows the NEXT route's doc comment, which is where the write vocabulary came from. One character of regex discipline. Building `cloud/`'s first AST check for a tie is pure cost, and there is no Credo in `cloud/`. |
| D46 | **The `62` census is NOT a phantom — it is a SECOND CORRECT POPULATION. Do not "retire" it; SEE it** | `56` = block-form `^  get "`. `62` = 56 + **6 parenthesized one-liners** (`get("/", do: send_dashboard(conn))` at `main:494/495/502/510/6314/6315`). Both reproduce on `origin/main` by grep. This is a live blind spot, not trivia: a `^  get "` regex is **invisible to 6 real routes today**, so a future side-effecting GET written in the parenthesized form would never enter the census. The pin must use the moduledoc test's `[\s(]+` form and see all 62. D34's `56/50/5/45` reproduces byte-identically and stands. |
| D47 | **The 45-writer floor does NOT become 44 when the SSE slice lands** | Refuted by running the identical enumerator on both trees: both give **session = 45**. `require_user_sse` tries `Auth.bearer_token(conn)` **first** and still calls `verify_user_session_token`, which still calls `touch_last_used`. `consume_sse_ticket` is an **additional fallback branch, not a replacement** — and it makes the route *worse*: `Repo.update(… revoked_at)` is a harder write than a timestamp touch. |
| D48 | **The SSE mint's unbounded growth is REAL and its shape is a REAPER, not a throttle** | Proven by run, not grep-absence: 3 mints for one user → **3 rows** (non-superseding by design, to avoid the two-tab eviction storm D28/D10 exist to prevent); consuming one leaves the count at **3** (soft-marks `revoked_at`, never deletes); **15 consecutive mints → 15 rows, all 200, zero 429**. No worker in `cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/workers/` references `UserToken`; no Oban crontab entry mentions `sse`. Reaper, not throttle, for three reasons: (a) the sibling defect D15 was paid with a reaper (`oauth_state_reaper`), and `device_auth_reaper` is the doubled precedent on main; (b) this surface's existing throttles (`@confirm_throttle` 1/300s, `@change_email_throttle` 3/3600s) guard **email DELIVERY**, a different justification than a bare authenticated row insert; (c) a per-user throttle risks 429-ing a legitimate second tab's reconnect — reintroducing exactly the failure mode the non-superseding mint was designed around. The row's 60s TTL already bounds its useful life, so growth is purely hygiene. |
| D49 | **`__css_check` E2 is NOT extended. The ruling is NO — and the fence for this instance is ALREADY BUILT by the sibling** | Both shapes were built and mutation-killed. Option A (a `__app.test.mjs` assertion calling the real `liveDotState` and checking each returned state has a `.live-chip[data-state="X"]` rule) is 26 lines. Option B is 35 lines and is **not an "extension" of E2 at all** — E2's technique is literal class-string extraction and has no path to attribute values fed by a variable, so any attribute check in `__css_check.mjs` is a bespoke parallel bolt-on with its own regex. Decisively: **PR #5377's `-r` branch already ships the equivalent, stronger fence** (`liveness chip: app.css carries a paint rule for EVERY chip state` plus a CLOSED-enum test pinning the return set), with its own documented mutation-kill, and it never touches `__css_check.mjs`. A second Option-A test would be duplicate coverage of the identical `liveDotState`/`app.css` pair. What remains is the **header disclaimer + the recorded ruling**. Correct the count while you are there: there are **4** `setAttribute("data-*")` sites, not 3 (the missed one is `app.js:16178 coherenceStampTheme`), and **3 of 4 are `data-theme`/`data-bp-theme`, already covered by E5's contrast engine** — only `data-state` is genuinely E2-blind. Known granularity limit, measured: both shapes prove SELECTOR-PREFIX presence, not per-property survival — deleting one of a state's two rules reds neither. |

**HIGH-FLIP-RISK independently re-derived (not a re-read):** the reachability claim — a slug-less expired-session 401 reaches `submitPasswordChange`'s render because `noBounce:true` bypasses `api()`'s auto-bounce — is CONFIRMED at emit-site level. `router.ex:1932` runs `Auth.require_user` first; on a dead token that halts via `unauthorized/1` → `json_halt(conn, 401, %{error: "unauthorized"})` (auth.ex:506), slug-less; the password check emits `%{error: "invalid_current_password"}` at router.ex:1961; `api()` gates its bounce `res.status === 401 && !opts.noAuth && !opts.noBounce` (app.js:139) so with `noBounce:true` both 401s return to the caller's else. Pre-fix bytes falsely accused the slug-less one. Mutation-proof re-run: reverting app.js to the bare `r.status === 401 ? "Current password is wrong."` arm reds the harness (# fail 1). A genuinely independent second reviewer remains owed per D887, but this reviewer's own re-derivation agrees with the builder's.

### Wave 67 — THE CONSOLE CAN UNMAKE WHAT IT MADE, AND EVERY WORD IT SAYS ABOUT DOING SO IS ONE THE PLANE ACTUALLY SAID (build in flight)

**Paper:** `cloud-console-hardening-wave-67-2026-08-10`. **This charter PR carries D811-D827.** Ceiling
was D810; wave 67 mints from D811. Everything below was re-derived on `origin/main` `f53167087a` — note
the tree moved twice under this wave (`8a8a2fdd` → `f53167087a`, the second move being deploy-reliability's
#11537, which **changes how a task read collapses `drafts.` twins and therefore how this epic's own child
count is derived**; re-derive it, never carry a number across that boundary).

**THE GAP, MEASURED AND NOT OVERSOLD.** `app.js` issues **14 `api("DELETE"…)` calls and not one is
`/v1/sites/:id`** (the near-miss at `:13845` is `/github`), and `teardown_failed` appears **0 times in
23,410 lines**. The console cannot delete a site at all. **There is therefore no live victim, because
there is no live path** — this is argued as a correctness gap and never sold as an outage. What raises
the stakes is what sits behind it: a route already correct and already typed (BOX FIRST — `Registry.delete_site`
fires only in the `:ok` arm, so a failed teardown never orphans a still-serving box behind a deleted
registration), carrying **eleven distinguishable envelopes nobody has ever been able to read**, and a
route comment that says in writing the refusal *"has no console surface at all yet."*

**THE ATTACK ON THIS DIRECTION IS CORRECT AND IS ABSORBED STRUCTURALLY, NOT RHETORICALLY.** An epic whose
whole discipline is "the console stops lying" drifts the moment it starts shipping capability. The
delete control is admitted **only as the CARRIER for honesty deliverables that cannot exist without it**,
and the reviewer's test is mechanical: strike the button from the diff and see whether they survive. A
reader for eleven refusal envelopes that ALREADY SHIP does not. A success sentence that stops asserting a
teardown the plane may not have performed does not. **That is the standard the next feature-shaped
proposal gets measured against too, and most will fail it.**

**THE VERIFICATION ROUND OVERTURNED THE CROWN'S OWN CENTREPIECE, AND THE WAVE IS BETTER FOR IT (D811).**
The direction's producer field is DEAD: `sites.barkpark_id` is `NOT NULL` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so
`is_nil(bp)` is unreachable, `box_present` has been a constant `true` since it was written, and the
"there was no box to tear down" sentence describes a state the schema forbids. Shipping it would have
minted a NEW vacuous reader **inside the wave that exists to kill vacuous readers**. The crown is now a
pure caller + reader living entirely in `cloud/priv/static/`, which also makes the `sites/deploy.ex`
fence dispute moot for it (D825) instead of arbitrated. Two further premises failed smoke and became
findings: the "false-done" is an honest documented dedupe (D823), and the "two receipt corrections" is
one (D812). **Six consecutive waves have now overturned a headline they were handed.**

**THE WAVE — 2 slices build this run, 3 are deferred to round 2 by the sequenced-rounds law.** The 502 copy fix (D814 Option A) is NOT a sixth slice: it rides S3, which already owns `deploy.ex` and the rollback-copy leak, so the fact keeps one owner.

**Paper:** `cloud-console-hardening-wave-55-2026-08-08`. **Charter PR carries D629-D643.** Every baseline below was

ACTOR that runs on it, the EFFECT that actor can produce. The console prints all three over the `suspended` column; the
plane holds none. Wave 54 proved the EFFECT is one `Repo.update_all` of four columns. This wave takes the structure:

DOWNSTREAM of an archive job kind that does not exist). No env-var deletion (D639: the cost premise is refuted; the
recommendation is four comment retractions, handed over as one line, not a fifth deferral).

### Wave 54 — THE LIFECYCLE-STATE REGISTER: a state the console renders as an operational fact must be produced by an action the plane performs (build in flight)

**THE CROWN.** The console paints `Suspended`/`Stopped`, removes Open Studio, and promises *"The server is stopped, not destroyed. Everything comes back exactly as it was the moment payment succeeds."* The entire mechanism is one UPDATE of three columns. Nothing stops a box, nothing fences traffic, nothing revokes access — three mint/reveal routes still hand out live credentials for a suspended instance — and suspension's only real effect is that the control plane stops WATCHING the box, leaving it unmonitored, unpatched, publicly serving, and still billing the operator. Confirmed as a mechanism (D617), keyed on `(state, reason)` because there are two producers and three reasons behind one painted state (D618), and **latent as an event** — prod has zero suspended rows across 27 teams, so this hardens the register before its first customer and every artifact says so in the present tense.

### Wave 53 — THE CUSTODY REGISTER: believing the promise costs you something you cannot take back (build in flight)

*(Union rider, wave 69 / #10766: wave 53 MERGED 2026-08-08 — #10725/#10726/#10727/#10728, review log #10729; round 2 dispatches in wave 54. #10766 recorded this by rewriting the heading above; the union keeps main's line byte-intact and adds this rider instead — pure-addition doctrine, D844.)*

instrument needs one, against live prod Postgres (`cloud-db-1`), against a LIVE managed box over SSH, or against the
live GitHub API — never the ~580-behind primary checkout.

**The axis, six waves deep.** Wave 46 took a control behind a drawer; 47 the first screen a member sees; 48 the
surface speaking for a third party; 49 the register where a lie costs money; 51 the register where the console is the
only witness; 52 the register where the failure has no surface at all. **53 is the step out from there: the register
where BELIEVING THE PROMISE MAKES YOU WORSE OFF THAN NOT HAVING IT.** A missing email is an absence. A secret you
hand over because a screen told you it would be delivered is an ACT — you took a live production credential out of
somewhere safe and put it somewhere it does nothing. The promise does not merely fail to help; it induces the
exposure it implies it manages. Custody is what the plane does with a thing after you give it up.

**The crown, and it is proven at L1 in three layers.** The environment-variables surface promises a custody and a
delivery the plane has no wiring for. Six surfaces assert it (`app.js:19941`, `:20046`, `index.html:479`,
`env_var.ex`, and `worker.go:175`'s own comment naming *"the same sanctioned crossing as env/credentials"* — prose
citing a field its struct lacks). The control plane honours the first half at `router.ex:10741`. The worker has no
field: the EXACT bytes the CP emits, fed through `JobSpec`'s real decode, lose the secret with no error and no log
line, while strict decode of those same bytes returns `json: unknown field "env"`. A live managed box carries 17
`.env` keys, all platform; its running process environ carries the same 17; and the DEPLOYED provisioner binary has
exactly one `json:"env"`, travelling the other way. The green test certifies exactly the half that works.
D604-D606 hold the crown, D607-D608 bind the guard, D609 hands round 2 to the lead.

**What this wave says that this epic has never said.** D613: the security register is LARGELY HONEST. Revocation
lands on request N+1, the PAT carve-out is deliberate and tested, a password change revokes more than it promises,
the SSE ticket burn is `FOR UPDATE`-locked and matched-row-only, and *append-only* is an immutability claim that
holds under a real trigger. Operator impersonation does not exist to audit. Three divergences survive and each is
placed at its true level — one LATENT (D612), one measured at the wire (D611), one already filed elsewhere.

**And the epic turns its own thesis on its own instruments.** D610: the audit census excuses four verbs with
rationales that are INERT STRINGS, three of them false against routes on the same tree — a losable instrument armed
with a certified false absence, which is worse than a bare producerless name. D614: `sh scripts/required-checks.test.sh`
exits **0** after running 68 of 170 assertions. D615: the ledger arrears is 23 rows, not 5, and four of the
instruments the chore would reach for are wrong.

### Wave 51 — THE RECORD: the Timeline names events nothing can produce, and the audit trail refuses a destructive one it already labels (build in flight)

**Paper:** `cloud-console-hardening-wave-51-2026-08-08`. **Charter PR carries D575-D587.** Everything below was re-derived by RUNNING
inside a full-tree `git archive origin/main` at `ca5bc5429`, never a worktree — except the Elixir blast radius and the
required-checks suite, which need a real `.git` (see the extract trap below).

**THE ORDERING LAW, ONE LEVEL OUT.** 46 took a control behind a drawer; 47 the first screen a member sees; 48 the surface speaking
for a third party; 49 the register where a wrong number costs money; 50 the promise about a future the payer had already paid for.
51 is **the register where the user cannot check the claim at all, because the console is the only witness there is.** A price can be
checked against a card statement; a refusal by clicking; a backup promise on the day you need it. A timeline and an audit trail are
self-certifying — their silence is indistinguishable from nothing having happened.

**THE CROWN.** The instance Timeline's event vocabulary is wrong in BOTH directions. `Registry.record_event/3` has exactly four
non-test call sites and they write `health`, `space`, `verify`, `status`; `backup`, `tls` and `content` have ZERO producers anywhere
in the plane, in the entire history of `main` (D579). The console renders all three as first-class record entries — `TLV_EVENT_TITLES`
gives them human titles, `tlvVerdictOf` (`app.js:10389`) carries a `backup` branch that answers *"completed"*, and the empty state
tells a brand-new owner in the console's own voice that *"backups"* will appear here. And the inverse: `space` IS produced and is
ABSENT from the title map, so a live event renders as a raw slug in the feed the console calls the instance's incident home.
Reachability is settled by reading the route: `GET /v1/barkparks/:id/events` (`router.ex:7967`) opens with bare `Auth.require_user`
plus a team scope — plain member, any team, every newly-launched instance.

**THE GUARD IS THE DELIVERABLE, AND IT IS THREE-ARMED (D575).** Bidirectional or tautology, side A the JavaScript, per the BINDING
D341 — whose decisive negative control was reproduced one-for-one on the fixed tree: injecting `moonphase` into `app.js` ALONE reds

### Wave 44 — the members surface stops offering what the server refuses, and both instruments that certified it learn to lose (build in flight)

**The frame.** Wave 43's crown MERGED (`#10199`/`#10200`/`#10201`/`#10202`), so `scenarios.mjs`'s `me(teamName, onb, role)` now mints `teams[]`, `team_authority` and a settable actor role — the dependency that stopped wave 43 from crowning the live lie is discharged. This wave takes it. `origin/main` was `ba712a4b2` for the whole survey/verify round and moved to `46b5373ed` (#10207, the papers reader theme toggle) while this charter was being written — every anchor was RE-VERIFIED at the new head and every one still holds, because `app.js`'s newest commit is still `d2a721ba2` and `breakpoint-sweep.test.mjs` still asserts `r.total, 106` / `r.residue, 81`. It is FULLY GREEN on its own head (29 check-runs, zero failures, one skip; the fourth required context, `PR references an active task`, is pull_request-only and can never appear on a push head — that absence is expected, not a jam).

**The lie, re-derived.** `app.js:18477 memberRowHtml` → `:18478 canManage = assignableRoles(ctx.role).length > 0`. `assignableRoles` (`:18417`) takes ONE argument, the actor's role; the target's role reaches only the chip and a `data-role` attribute. The server answers a RANK-RELATIVE question and answers it DIFFERENTLY FOR THE TWO VERBS: `accounts.ex:1722` `actor_role == "owner" or outranks?(...)` (owner escape hatch) vs `accounts.ex:1801` `not self? and not outranks?(...)` (no hatch, after `Authz.can_grant?/3` which never consults the target's current role at all). So an acting ADMIN is offered `Change role` and `Remove` on the team OWNER's row and on every peer-admin row — four controls the server 403s `reason: "outranked"` — and an acting OWNER may REMOVE a peer owner but may NOT CHANGE their role. Two predicates, or the fix is a new lie. Per D428 (an ONLY-clause over seven lifecycle-rail verbs) and D484, the remedy on this settings surface is OMIT, never a disabled ghost.

**What measurement moved, and it moved the crown's SHAPE five times.** (1) `app.js:18480` ALREADY suppresses every self control via `(canManage && !isSelf)`, so the second asymmetry is invisible in shipped UI — and the honest fix ships `Change role` on the self row while still withholding `Remove` (D492, variant B, chosen because the pure mirror reds the merge-blocking smoke). (2) An unrankable TARGET ranks 0 = BELOW everyone; the "fail closed on the target" instruction is REFUTED and would ship a false refusal (D493). (3) `last_owner` is a **409 STATE** refusal, not authority — omission keys on 403-BY-AUTHORITY only, so on a one-owner team the owner-self control stays rendered. (4) A role-only admin scenario is DOA: `me()` hardcodes `usr_ada` and `teamMembers[0]` IS `usr_ada`/owner, so members-populated renders BYTE-IDENTICALLY at 4220 vs 4220 with an identical wire-call list; only moving the ACTOR to `usr_lin` renders the lie (D494, and this is why the fixture is a separate round-2 slice). (5) `assignableRoles` has FOUR identical `canManage` sites (`:18478`, `:18499`, `:18518`, `:18575`) and only the first is rank-relative — a mechanical conversion of all four breaks invitations, which are NOT rank-relative server-side.

**Two premises failed smoke and are recorded as findings, not foundations.** D448's "an OWNER acting on a peer owner reaches `outranked` on REMOVE" is false of DELETE and the false sentence is IN THE SHIPPED SOURCE at `app.js:264-266` (D495). D483's zero-scenario ruling rests on a collision that MERGED hours before this wave opened (D494). A third, harder finding: the crux disagreement the console is about to mirror is pinned by NOTHING on the server side (D496) — 10 of 21 relation×verb cells are true-but-unguarded, and the two files the wave's own MUST-RUN named contain zero assertions on either verb.

**Two more rendered lies found while tracing, both in the file the crown already opens, both riding `w44-s1`.** `app.js:19938-19941`: the `#members-invite` click handler is `var c = membersContext(); if (c) openInviteModal(c);` with **no else** — the button is un-hidden at render under a `grant` band, `membersContext()` is re-evaluated at CLICK time, and its `stale` arm (`:14252`) is a live `localStorage` read, so a visible button can produce literally nothing: no modal, no toast, no refusal. And `app.js:18696 openRoleModal` builds its `<option>` list from `assignableRoles(ctx.role)` alone and marks `selected` only on `r === currentRole`; with no match the browser preselects the FIRST option, so an admin opening it on the owner's row sees a dialog that has already silently staged a demotion they never chose.

**Ledger hygiene this wave pays.** `cch-w43-s3` sits `in_progress` at 7/8 with its PR `#10201` merged as `f2e3283bf` (an ancestor of `origin/main`) — a stale-open row of exactly the class this epic polices; closed this wave. `task-ed706f4e1c616f89` asks for two refusal sentences that ALREADY SHIP at `app.js:272-273`; closed. `cch-w42-s3` becomes `w44-s1` (re-briefed, not re-filed): its AC1/AC4/AC6 are rewritten, AC8 downgraded (D482 is the run-proof), and **AC9 is STRUCK** — it forbids exactly the admin fixture wave 44 ships. `cch-w43-bl-binding-census-arity-arm` becomes `w44-s2`, `cch-w43-bl-me-census-onboarding-subtree` becomes `w44-s3`, `cch-no-admin-fixture-in-the-preview-corpus` becomes `w44-s4`. ### Wave 41 — the console stops inventing who you are (build in flight)

**The frame.** Six waves made the console honest about a NO it already received. Wave 41 moves to the
larger lie, the one told *before* any request leaves the browser: the console decides what you may do
using a rule it invented and the server never stated. The `owner|admin` set is written out as a literal
expression **six** times in `app.js` (`2378 providerCanWrite`, `3517 notifCanManage`, `3945
canMintAnyAbility`, `6045 canManageOnboarding`, `13406 billingCanManage`, `18004 assignableRoles` —
every anchor re-derived; the brief's 3518/3946 were one line high), and the same rule exists twice more
on the server with member<admin<owner rank encoded independently in `TeamMembership.@ranks` and
`Authz.@rank`. Eight statements of "who may", agreeing only by hand, with nothing asserting they agree.
Meanwhile `/v1/me` already sends `role` for the current team and `teams[].role` — the ACCEPT side of
authority is on the wire and unread, while the REFUSE side is what six waves have been repairing.

**What measurement moved.** The direction survived its sharpest attack: the **team axis is clean**
(D467) and the **two server predicates agree on every reachable value including nil and off-ladder
strings**, so the collapse is behaviourally free across all 36 invocations and priority (3) is a
pin-the-agreement job. But three of five briefed priorities changed shape. The lifecycle rail is
**7/7 unpredicated on main, not 3/7**, and it belongs to open #9955 (D458). Priority (4)'s
"extend the census so an unbound elevated write cannot ship" is **false on #10085's own HEAD** — a new
unbound write ships rc 0 if you add a PIN row and bump `EXPECT` — and its honest form is a
frozen-legacy ratchet that needs its own fixture mode (D460). And the admin-limb fixture is cheaper
and safer in the unit seam than in the four-way-contended scenario census (D461, D464). One premise
died outright: `scope:"token"` is PAT-only and can never reach a browser, so the bounded-label echo is
dead copy, not a defect (D463).

**The cut.** Round 1: `w41-s1` proves the two server predicates single over the FULL role domain with
a mutation only it catches; `w41-s2` makes `/v1/me` state a team-scoped authority fact and brings the
owner/admin/member/teamless pins the endpoint has never had; `w41-s3` gives the four `owner|admin`
predicates a unit guard that reds when the admin limb is dropped. Round 2, dispatched by the lead after

`w41-s5` (the `LEGACY_UNPREDICATED` ratchet) after **#10085**. Paper:
`cloud-console-hardening-wave-41-2026-08-07`.

(#9955's), the 18-affordance binding fix (`cch-w36-bl`, whose OMIT default D428 fixes), the two

### Wave 40 — a refusal renders what was proved, and nothing else (build in flight)

**The frame.** Waves 34-39 climbed one ladder: the console asserts a STATE it never received, a CAUSE
it never determined, an AUTHORITY it never checked, then answers all three three-valued. Wave 40 takes
the sentence at the bottom of that ladder. One line of `app.js` is this epic's most productive liar —
`ERRORS.forbidden: "Only the team owner can manage billing."` — and three waves have been buying it
back one screen at a time. Add the fences up and nobody has said the consequence out loud: **the
billing sentence can now only ever render where it is false** (D447). It is not a copy bug on four
screens; it is a default pointed the wrong way, and the epic has been paying interest on it since
wave 34.

**Finished feels like this.** A person refused anywhere in the console reads exactly what the server
proved — the authority it wanted, the cause it named, or an honest *"you don't have permission to do
that"* — never a confident sentence about a screen they are not on. An admin removing a peer admin is
told they were outranked, not told about billing. An admin refused across tenants is not told they
are not an admin. A permanent authority determination is not sold as *"momentarily unavailable"*. And
the next engineer who writes a confident sentence the envelope cannot support gets a red PR instead
of a wave-45 backlog row.

**How the direction survived contact, and where it did not.** The sharpest attack on the inversion —
that it trades five wrong screens for one degraded right screen — **died exactly as predicted**: all
three billing routes gate first-statement on `require_primary_team_owner`, so `forbiddenEvidenceCopy`
wins and the inversion structurally cannot reach a billing screen; pin #911 reds on its BARE arm, not
its owner arm, which is the proof. But the FINDING MOVED (D448): the billing sentence's live traffic
is not the three bare literals at all — it is two reason-carrying member-management refusals with no
written arm, and the two reachable bare literals are shadowed by authored local copy the inversion
can never touch. That turned "S1+S2 must ship together" from an assertion into a measurement, and
added a third leg. Two of the direction's five S2 rows were **already paid** (#9848 `newLaunch`,
#9851 `operatorConfirmBrake`) and are not re-cut; the biggest surviving one (`attachDomain`, five
server slugs collapsed into one false sentence) is **fenced off** inside #9955's band and filed.

**Six slices.**

### Wave 38 — the authority answer becomes three-valued, and stops being sold before it is asked (build in flight)

**The frame.** Waves 34-37 climbed one ladder: the console asserts a STATE it never received, then a
CAUSE it never determined, then an AUTHORITY it never checked. Wave 38 takes the last rung and adds
the rung above it: the console must answer the authority question the **same way in both moments** —
before the click and after it — and it must be able to say **"I don't know yet"**, because it
frequently doesn't.

**Finished feels like this.** A member opens an instance they do not administer. The lifecycle rail is
still THERE — a control that disappears is indistinguishable from a missing feature — but
Decommission / Roll back / Self-update / Attach domain are **disabled**, with one muted line beneath:
*"You need the admin role on this team — an admin on this team can grant it."* That is not new copy;
it is `FORBIDDEN_ROLE_COPY.admin`, the exact string the server's own 403 already produces through
`friendly()`. And while `/v1/me` is in flight or failed, the rail says **CHECKING** — never refused.

**THE CONDITION THAT SHAPED THE CUT.** GitHub Actions is in a major outage; 22 PRs are open and 15 are
finished wave work on queued checks, including all six wave-37 slices (#9917-#9922) and charter #9857.
Nothing is blocked on design or build capacity. So: **three slices, two new code PRs, zero pushes to
any branch whose gate is queued** — a push cancels the queued run and re-queues a full matrix, which
is the single most expensive thing this wave could do. Depth was bought only where it is free
(criteria, mutations, verify-fleet re-derivation).

**THE THREE SLICES.**

| # | Slice | Task | PR? | Model | Round |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| S3 | The spec-gate packet, prepared and costed — and the roster stops lying about its own size | `cch-w38-s3-spec-gate-packet-and-roster-disposition` | none | opus | 1 |

**S1 is the crown**, and D428/D429/D430/D431/D432 are its whole design: a single three-valued
`instanceAdminAuthority()` (grant / refuse / unknown) built on `meState()`, threaded **into**
`lifecycleActionsModel` as an explicit argument so the harness can see it at all (D430 — the census
structurally cannot), rendering the shipped-but-never-reached `.inst-life-disabled` grammar, plus the
three post-click arms without which the promise is undone one click later. The unknown arm is a HARD
criterion, not a nicety: predicating seven sites two-valued would manufacture seven fresh instances of

that on a failed `/v1/me` a real owner is told, as flat fact, *"Only the team owner can manage

### Wave 36 — authority is answered, not guessed (build in flight)

**The frame, one rung up the same ladder.** Wave 34: the console asserts a STATE it never received.
Wave 35: it asserts a CAUSE it never determined. Wave 36 takes the axis both landed on without
naming — **WHO**. Authority is the one thing this product decides about a person on every request,
and it is currently decided TWICE by two mechanisms that never speak: the browser GUESSES what you
may do so it can draw the screen, and the server DETERMINES it and throws the determination away.
`data.required` and `data.scope` appear **zero** times in the 20,545-line `app.js`.

all merged at 11:46Z on 2026-08-06, so `Auth.forbidden/2` is live at `auth.ex:502` with seven

(`cch-w35-s4`) is now **client-only round-1 work**. Its stated blocker is gone.

alert rail as a subsystem**, and **the evidence survives the failure**. Wave 34 takes the shape
underneath all four: a surface has three things it can say about a live thing — nothing has happened
yet, I have stopped hearing from it, it finished — and this product ships renderers that resolve the
middle one into one of the outer two. **The console is not wrong about data it HAS; it asserts a
state it never RECEIVED.**

a required-gate disclosure whose headline says the opposite of its body on all four gates (D387), and

it with the wish's other half, **a gate telling a MERGE something it cannot support.**

deployments end on a non-terminal console line and the panel prints a bare count as though that were the
whole log** — across NINE sites, at 7/day and falling. s3 is cut to that, plus a drop counter the two
at-cap rows keep non-vacuous. See D373.

### Wave 32 — the alert rail stops lying, end to end

Wave 30 killed **the affordance with no mechanism** (a promise nothing can keep). Wave 31 took its mirror,
**the mechanism that acts and does not disclose**. Wave 32 stops hunting single strings and takes a whole
SUBSYSTEM: the notification/alert rail, from producer → routing vocabulary → channel fan-out → the withhold
decision → the person's own receipt. The rail earns the depth because **a notification is the only thing this
product says to you when you are NOT looking at it.** Every other divergence in this epic needs a person present
at a screen; this one lies while the customer sleeps. That is the Kinsta/Vercel bar: you either trust the alert
or you sit and watch the dashboard, and Barkpark Cloud has not earned the first option.

Five hops were framed; verification kept three, refuted one and replaced one with a better defect.

1. **PRODUCE** — a Slack-only team is never told its trial ends and its instance is torn down. CONFIRMED, and
   it is four sites, not one: the vocabulary, the routing rule, the missing `render.ex` arm (a routed teardown
   warning ships `"Event: trial_expiring for <team>."` at `:info` — Discord GREEN) and the console copy that
   now describes the wrong mechanism. Routing rule settled by a four-variant run (**D359**); `general` is dead
   and is deleted rather than routed (**D360**).
2. **CONTROL** — a checkbox labelled "Email alerts enabled" silently kills Slack, Discord, Telegram, Pushover
   and every webhook. CONFIRMED — and the sharper lie is the one button whose job is to answer *"will I be
   told?"*: it bypasses the mute entirely and writes, on the wire and into the delivery log, *"If you can read
   this, the channel works."* Ruled a transport probe that must disclose, not a policy probe that refuses
   (**D361**).
3. **FAN OUT** — `enqueue_channel/4`'s `|> Oban.insert()` result is discarded inside a bare `for`. LIVE.
   Its sibling, `dispatch_site_event/3`'s `else -> :ok`, was already adjudicated CONSENTED by D349(b) and is
   NOT re-filed.
4. **WITHHOLD** — the reaper caps `deployment_failed` fan-out at 25/sweep and writes the suppression to a
   Logger line. CONFIRMED verbatim — and a withhold was IMPOSSIBLE to represent. `suppressed` lands, server
   and console in one slice, with no migration (**D362**); the population is seven, six unconsented, with the
   lens stated (**D363**); only one of the three alleged "pinned lies" is actually a lie (**D364**).
5. **RECEIPT** — REFUTED. The admin/user asymmetry does not exist; admin is the house rule and D349(a) already
   ruled it correct. The better defect underneath it is the moduledoc route table, which tells a CLI, an SDK
   and a cold agent the wrong tier on **three** rows — with a census that is vacuously green over 36% of the
   table unless it is built carefully (**D365**).

Two rows the direction put in scope come OUT on measurement: the delivery-log index/retention row, whose
performance framing is refuted and whose `id`-in-the-index prescription is a pessimization (**D366**), and the
proposed `s7` changeset clamp as a standalone safety gate for the member read (**D368**). What replaces the
latter is a real, live, production-measured leak of four rows carrying a Vault-sealed IP address (**D367**).

### Wave 31 — the system decided and did not say

Wave 30 killed the affordance with no mechanism: **a promise nothing can keep.** Wave 31 takes its exact
mirror, which is the larger half of what remains open here: **THE MECHANISM THAT ACTS AND DOES NOT
DISCLOSE.** The control plane makes a real decision — it withholds an alert, it caps a fan-out at 25, it
swallows an event on a deleted site, it prints a masked secret into a log, it collapses three transport
faults into one `status 0`, it demotes an owner and revokes nothing — and the only party who could act on
that decision is the one never told. A promise nothing can keep and a decision nobody discloses are the
same lie with opposite polarity; the epic's triage predicate covers both, and only one had been paid.

The discipline that rides with it is wave 30's best lesson one level up: **DISCLOSE AT THE SEAM, NOT AT
THE EDGE.** S5 fixed six blaming call sites; the lever was `api()` itself. The withhold branches want one
`suppressed` status, not ten bespoke log lines. The relay-host leak wants ONE classifier at
`record_delivery/5`, not a filter at every read. The demotion wants a rank drop, not a fourteenth role
literal. The escape ratchet wants a source set that sees one call frame down, not a fifteenth
hand-declared path.

**AND THE WAVE TURNED ITS OWN PREDICATE ON ITSELF, WHICH IS THE STORY.** The centrepiece as filed would
have shipped three lies: a person-facing claim on an **ADMIN-gated** surface (D349a), a `suppressed` row
that renders today as a blue *"Pending"* pill on a surface nobody re-derived (D349f), and a traced branch
**no reader query can return** (D349b). Its own boundary slice's population was **inverted** — three
blaming sentences, not twenty-nine vague ones (D353) — and the strongest of the three,
`webhookMutationError`, appears in **no filed row** and is being propagated as the console's exemplar of
honest copy. And a live secret leak was found *inside* the fix: `delivery_json/1`'s *"Nothing here is a
secret"* is FALSE for admins today (D350). Verification did not confirm the plan. It amputated it, and
each amputation is a finding.

law.** Five of eight are person-facing; the ratio floor is met on merit.

### Wave 30 — an affordance with no mechanism behind it is a lie, and a census is the guard that can lose

Twenty-nine waves hunted claim/reality divergences one string at a time. They are all instances of one
shape, and this wave names the shape and closes it as a class: **A SURFACE OFFERS SOMETHING — DOES A
MECHANISM EXIST THAT CAN DELIVER IT?** Where the answer is no, the surface is lying, whether the surface
is a toggle a customer flips, an error a control plane returns, or an instruction a merge-blocking gate
prints at a human at 2am. The signature artifact is a guard CLASS, not eight unrelated guards — the
**CENSUS GUARD**: it derives its expectation from the surface itself rather than a list somebody must
remember to update, it takes its two sides from INDEPENDENT sources, and it is mutation-proved by
injecting a promise into ONE side only. Derive, don't declare.

**The wave's own sixth standing clause, and it is structural, not advisory:** every census guard takes
its two sides from INDEPENDENT sources — one from the surface a person sees (rendered bytes, printed
error text, the UI's own label list), one from production call sites — and it is mutation-proved in
BOTH arms. A census that stays green when a fake toggle is added, or when a producer with no surface row
is added, does not ship. D341 records the negative control that earned this clause: the cheap
Elixir-on-Elixir variant was BUILT and stayed green against a lie injected into `app.js` alone.

Six slices, five in round 1, one deferred to round 2. Person-facing : instrument ratio holds at 4:2.

| # | slice | round | task |

| S3 | the escape ratchet sees one call frame down; its floor stops being unable to fire | **2, after S1** | `cch-w30-s3-escape-ratchet-transitive-and-per-idiom-floor` |
| S4 | the blocking merge gate stops printing an escape it cannot honour | 1 | `cch-w30-s4-merge-lane-false-escape` |

Wave 20's thesis: **KILL THE SEQUENCER AND PAY THE SCREENS.** The one-hand baseline law is real, but
its benefit is the correctness of ONE integer and its price has been three waves of unpaid screens on
the product's most-seen surfaces. D230-D232 replace polite queuing with a machine-checked
prohibition: exactly one named holder (s8, measured — D230 proves the direction seated the only
net-zero slice), three abstainers whose diffs may not contain the file, D202's conflicting prose
clause waived, and each abstainer's own gate criterion asserting its measured mismatch so the wave
PRICES itself as a side effect of gating itself. The lead's corrective re-run on the integrated tree
becomes mandatory rather than contingent.

What verification then bought that neither the wish nor the direction had: **s8 was not dispatchable
at all** (D233 — its strict criterion and its rc=0 criterion are mutually unsatisfiable on today's
bytes, with a driven escape, a lower-bound requirement, and a `BREAKPOINTS` debt none of its ten
criteria mention); **s6 reds two committed instruments on arrival, one of them this epic's own seal
predicate** (D234); **both filed fourth-seat candidates are subsumed by measurement, and the seat is
filled by a newly-driven defect in the same band rather than by reviving a subsumed row or inventing
one** (D235); and the four-way merge is clean **only** at assigned anchors, conflicting in BOTH shared
files if left to instinct (D236). Four of the wish's six items were already paid, already executed or
structurally blocked before a builder flew (D239, D223, D226) — which is itself the finding.

**Honesty tax, stated not hidden.** Every green this wave buys is font-conditional: D218 proved the
guard never awaits `document.fonts.ready` and never asserts which face resolved, so an rc=0 means
"green on this host with this face" and no more. The row is already filed (`task-d862cf7f8e1108c1`,
0/7, p1) and is NOT re-filed here; what wave 20 adds is the observation that `breakpoint-sweep.mjs` is
equally blind and that row covers only the guard. Second tax: `Console gate` is **not merge-blocking**
(D238), so this wave's CI-visible mutation pair buys EVIDENCE, not ENFORCEMENT — priced that way in
the Paper, with the one-line registration lever refused out loud rather than taken quietly.

### Wave 19 — the guard loses in CI, and the screens keep getting paid

Wave 18 gave `overflow-guard.mjs` a job after five waves of assertions sat in a file CI never ran.
The row that bought it is **not closed**, and its two open criteria are the whole point: the wiring
must be MUTATION-PROVEN — a deliberate regression turns the CI job red, and reverting turns it green.
The job exists (`console-harness.yml:487`, the 0/1/2 ladder, `Console gate`'s `needs:`). **What is
unproven is that it can LOSE.** A wiring slice that cannot be shown to fail is exactly the disease it
was written to cure.

Wave 19's thesis: **PROVE THE WIRING CAN LOSE, THEN SPEND THE PROOF.** After this wave, "the guard is
wired" stops meaning "a job exists" and starts meaning "we watched TWO CI contexts move together on a
deliberate break and back on its revert, and quoted both run ids." Verification then bought three
things the direction did not have (D217 `Console gate` is NOT merge-blocking, so the proof is
AGGREGATOR PROPAGATION and must say so; D218 the guard can FALSE-GREEN under a narrower font face,
which is the wave's headline finding; D219 the topbar band is 620 and not 430, which retires the
wish's own `BREAKPOINTS` obligation by measurement) and refuted one framing outright (D220 — the wrap
recipe the epic has copied three times DOES NOT FIX the fourth host, so D210's extraction trigger
fires on a host the extraction would misfix, and the answer is an instrument, not a refactor).

The standing test carries forward with wave 18's sharper edge: *a fix whose only guard is a sentence
is not fixed* — **and a guard no job runs is a sentence with a shebang.** Wave 19 adds the third
clause the font probe forced: **and a guard that cannot lose is a sentence with an exit code.**

Ratio: four person-facing slices, six person-hit defects (D227), none invented, and the operator pill
is EXCLUDED from the count by L1 evidence (D221) rather than argued into it. The baseline one-hand law
(D202) is the wave's only real sequencer — four slices want `cssom-heads.baseline`, so they run as a
chain (`s2 → s6 → s8 → s7`) and only `s2` builds this run.

### Wave 18 — the front screen, and the guard that proves it stays fixed

The most-seen surface in this product hides **66% of why an instance is degraded** — and on the
mixed fleet it hides **81%**. Five waves of person-facing fixes have shipped their proof into
`overflow-guard.mjs`, a 1131-line instrument that **no `run:` step has ever invoked**: the single
mention of it across `.github`, `scripts` and `Makefile` is a comment at `console-harness.yml:272`
whose own stated proof ("`grep -rn overflow-guard .github/` still exits 1") is falsified by that
comment containing the string. Wave 16's standing test was *a fix whose only guard is a sentence is
not fixed*; wave 18's successor is **A GUARD NO JOB RUNS IS A SENTENCE WITH A SHEBANG** — and the
front screen is the right place to prove it, because the most-seen fix in the product is the one that
most deserves to never regress.

**The wave's sharpest self-attack was refuted by running it (D208).** The fear that a
never-executed instrument reds `Console gate` on day one is false: the guard exits 0 on untouched
`origin/main` in 12.6s on a quiet host, `FLEET_KNOWN` is `[]` so the fail-closed allowlist cannot
fire, and deleting a merged remedy makes it lose at exit 1 naming the exact cell. Wiring is a
~20-line copy of an existing job, not a repair — but `console-gate` names its five upstreams BY HAND
and **omitting the `decide()` line is the one silent failure**, so the review instruction is a count
(D209).

sentence, and an instrument structurally unable to see the thing it certifies.

rewritten from "the floor is unprovable" (false) to "the floor's VALUE is unguarded from ~186 to 230
and at every width above 901" (measured). Both halves state which mutation they refuse, and every PR

wave wants ladder attribution anyway, the honest build is an `actor_user_id` column on `deployments`

recreate the duplicate-ownership defect that cancelling `gr-blk-vercel-checks-ungoverned` cured. The
diagnosis, run with `vercel inspect --logs --scope guerrilla` (the default scope
`frikk-jarls-projects` cannot see these deployments, which is probably why nobody got the log): six
`Module not found` on `@barkpark/react` and `@barkpark/core`, because their entry points are `./dist/*`,
`dist/` is gitignored, and nothing builds the workspace packages before `next build` — diff-independent,
hence red on every sha. The complete fix is `workspace:*` (in-tree precedent:
`apps/mobile/package.json:15-16`) **plus** a `prebuild` in `web/package.json`; `prebuild` alone leaves
2 errors because pnpm INJECTS a copy of `@barkpark/react` (it has peerDependencies + `files:[dist]`)
while `@barkpark/core` is symlinked and heals. Both red checks are two Vercel projects rooted at the
same `web/` directory — deleting one removes a permanent red with no code change.

  consequences that name only what was measured) wired to a Delete button placed LAST in the site

  is a pure exported status+data classifier over the envelope the route actually emits — 409

  refusal relaying the plane's own measured detail, a 422 TIMEOUT discriminated from that refusal by
  `detail` ALONE (status and code are byte-identical), a 502 wearing the console's own opener (D814),
  and the crash envelope. It reads singular `data.detail`, never calls `friendly()` (plural `detailS`),
  never gates on `data.ok`. No optimistic row removal; a failure sentence survives a modal dismissed
  mid-flight as a toast and a late success never navigates (D818); the 30s arm offers a Re-check that
